key_insight: GSH-initialized orientation-aware deep material networks compact crystal texture into fixed weighted orientations, improving stress and texture-evolution predictions while reducing online solution cost.
engineering_relevance: The approach enables texture-sensitive, two-scale component simulations at an estimated cost three to four orders of magnitude below concurrent full-field analysis.
method: Compress the initial RVE texture into 2^N weighted orientations using generalized spherical harmonics.
Fix initial material-node orientations and train only interaction directions.
Exploit binary-tree sparsity with structured LU factorization, reducing Newton-iteration cost from O(8^N) to O(2^N N^2).
evidence_signal: Tests against full-field simulations of two IN625 RVEs under isothermal and thermomechanical load–unload–reload paths showed improved stress and texture predictions, with normalized texture-difference indices below 0.03 in all cases at N=8.
watch_item: Validation covers two IN625 textures; broader material generalization remains unestablished, and GSH truncation order must be chosen for the network depth.
paper_title: From Compact Orientation Distributions to Texture Evolution: GSH-Initialized Orientation-Aware Deep Material Networks
